  • Sources indicate that the Grammy winner proved she’s just a girl who’s found a place in this world as an auntie as she and the 7-year-old cheered on her husband Travis Kelce during his Kansas City Chiefs’ Nov.
  • According to recent reports, during the matchup at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City—which marked Travis’ 100th regular season home game—the NFL star scored not one, but two career-defining touchdowns while dominating the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prepare for a few teardrops on your guitar after seeing Taylor Swift’s sweet moment with her niece Wyatt.

Sources indicate that the Grammy winner proved she’s just a girl who’s found a place in this world as an auntie as she and the 7-year-old cheered on her husband Travis Kelce during his Kansas City Chiefs’ Nov. 22 face-off against the Arizona Cardinals.

According to recent reports, during the matchup at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City—which marked Travis’ 100th regular season home game—the NFL star scored not one, but two career-defining touchdowns while dominating the field. In the game’s first quarter, his touchdown launched him into third place all-time for the most career touchdowns by an NFL tight end, which was followed by a second touchdown that marked his first two-touchdown game since 2022.

And it was clear that Taylor and Wyatt—the eldest daughter of the “Opalite” singer’s in-laws Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s four kids—were in a state of grace over the achievement as footage shared to social media Nov. 22 caught them in a sweet embrace after the second play.

The 36-year-old—donning a Chiefs windbreaker from Erin Andrews’ WEAR clothing line and her signature red lip—yelled in excitement from her suite as she hugged Wyatt from behind.

And it’s clear Wyatt was thrilled to have her aunt wrapped around her like a cardigan as she smiled wide.

Sources indicate that but they weren’t the only ones enchanted by Travis’ skills on the field. After all, the athlete did a little celebrating himself after his 22-yard touchdown reception, yelling “come on!” as he jumped up and down.

Sources indicate that the thrilling moment comes one week after Travis suffered an ankle injury that left him temporarily sidelined during his team's 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta Nov. 15.

In a recent development, thankfully, the 37-year-old made it clear he was Mr. Perfectly Fine after the ordeal.

"I'm all good," Travis told USA Today after the game. "I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them.".

"We had a lot of young guys step up," he added, "so it was really nice.".

It’s also always nice to see Taylor fulfill her auntie duties, which Travis recently admitted took his nieces a while to get used to.

“We had to break that habit of your daughters,” Travis noted on the Sept. 16 episode of his and Jason’s Fresh Heights podcast. “When they got to meet Aunt Tay Tay, they were calling her 'Taylor Swift.’”.

Industry observers note that in fact, Jason—who also shares daughters Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 20, months with Kylie—recalled them saying, “‘Taylor Swift, can I do this? Taylor Swift!’”.

And while they seem to be more comfortable with Taylor’s big reputation these days, Kylie shared that her little ones wanted the “Cardigan” singer to be a part of the family even before she wed their Uncle Trav this past July.

In a recent development, "They’re so excited they’re getting another aunt, and we could not be more excited for them and what the future holds," the Not Gonna Lie podcast host added on Good Morning America last September. "We love love, and we love Taylor and Trav.".

Keep reading for all the reasons sparks continue to fly for Taylor and Travis….

In a recent development, long before Taylor Swift's attendance at the Kansas City Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 game became one of the definitive pop culture moments of the year, Travis Kelce was an admirer of the Grammy winner.

The star tight end's interest in Taylor was first revealed by one of his teammates in a TikTok video posted by the Chiefs in August 2023 (which, in hindsight, was when the pair were secretly dating).

Before Travis could answer the prompt of who his celebrity crush was, wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling spilled, "Taylor Swift!".

Travis smiled at the camera before holding his finger up to his mustache, saying, "Alright now!".

Plus, Travis was just one of many celebs to attend Taylor's record-breaking Eras Tour even before the now-engaged duo kicked off their romance. But more on that enchanting moment in a bit...

Sources indicate that no. 2: He's Not Her Usual Type (on Paper).

While he does have that daydream look in his eyes (especially when he sees Taylor on the big-screen at one of his games), Travis stands out a bit when you look back at Taylor’s dating history.

She is typically attracted to creative types, including actors (Joe Alwyn, Jake Gyllenhaal, Taylor Lautner and Tom Hiddleston) and musicians (Calvin Harris, John Mayer, Harry Styles and, most recently, Matty Healy).

But perhaps that’s why her romance with the lighthearted and cheeky athlete—who signed an updated two-year deal with the Chiefs worth $34.25 million in 2024—feels like such a refreshing option for Taylor after her six-year uber-private relationship with Joe came to an end in April 2023.

Looks like the 10-time Pro Bowler’s wishes came true after he all but manifested his romance with the superstar through sheer will, determination and declarations of infatuation.

Travis publicly aired his failed attempt to shoot his shot and talk to Taylor when he attended the Kansas City stop on her Eras Tour July 7, 2023. As it turns out, he had a special gift for her: A friendship bracelet bearing his "number" that he hoped to give Taylor. (He wouldn't definitively say if it was his jersey number or phone number.).

Despite his claim that he was "disappointed" he failed to meet her after the concert, Taylor confirmed to TIME in December 2023 that she belatedly caught his podcast pass.

Recent findings suggest that "Travis very adorably put me on blast on his podcast, which I thought was metal as hell," she recalled. "We started hanging out right after that. So we actually had a significant amount of time that no one knew, which I'm grateful for, because we got to get to know each other.".

So, that whole theory about the Sept. 24 game being their first official hang? As Taylor clarified to TIME, "We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date.".

Since dating Travis, Taylor has been seen in public more frequently, including outings with friends in NYC and jubilant appearances at award demonstrates, like the 2023 MTV VMAs and the 2024 Grammys.

Sources indicate that but her most talked-about appearance? Sitting in Travis' suite at the Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 home game against the Chicago Bears.

Industry observers note that rather than shy away from the attention, Taylor cheered and screamed "Let's f--king go!" when Travis scored a touchdown. Like the public, even Travis admitted he was caught off-guard by Taylor accepting his invite.

"Shoutout to Taylor for pulling up, that was pretty ballsy," Travis mentioned days later on his Upcoming Heights podcast. "I just thought it was awesome how everyone in the suite had nothing but great things to say about her, the friends and family.".

"She looked amazing," he added. " It was definitely a game I will remember, that's for damn sure.".

Since then, Taylor and Travis have been photographed hand-in-hand on dates all around the world and have made multiple visits to a Christmas bar in Kansas City, where they were not shy about PDA.

And, after revealing to TIME that she retreated from the spotlight when Kim Kardashian's infamous leaked phone call in 2016, Taylor is going out tonight...and every night, if she wants to, thank you very much.

"Life is short," she said. "Have adventures. Me locking myself away in my house for a lot of years—I’ll never get that time back. I’m more trusting now than I was six years ago.”.

Industry observers note that no. 5: He Knows When to Pull Back.

According to recent reports, while Travis isn't afraid to spill some tea on his Sept. 27, 2023 podcast regarding his interactions with Taylor, he still expressed his boundaries about addressing his personal life moving forward.

In a recent development, "I know I brought all this attention to me," he explained. "I did the whole friendship bracelet thing and told everyone how butthurt I was that I didn't get to meet Taylor." However, he continued, he didn't proposal to give a full play-by-play of their relationship.

"What's real is that it is my personal life and I want to respect both of our lives," he explained. "I'm enjoying life and I sure as hell enjoyed this weekend. So everything moving forward, I think me talking about sports and saying 'alright nah' will have to be where I keep it.".

He doubled-down on his desire to play it cool in a November 2023 interview with the Wall Street Journal.

Recent findings suggest that "Everybody around me telling me: Don't f--k this up! And me sitting here saying: Yeah—got it," he told the outlet, before addressing the media attention. "That was the biggest thing to me: make sure I don't say anything that would push Taylor away.".

But that doesn't mean he's been able to resist publicly talking about his girlfriend—crediting her for the boost in sales of his jersey and calling her "amazing" after she was booed by Latest England Patriots fans at a December 2023 game.

"I've never been a man of words," he admitted to WSJ. "Being around her, seeing how smart Taylor is, has been f--king mind-blowing. I'm learning every day.".

Like Taylor, who is close with her parents, particularly her mother Andrea, Travis hails from a tight-knit fam, including his parents Ed and Donna Kelce.

Donna became a beloved public figure as the first mother to have two sons playing against each other in a Super Bowl, when Travis faced off against his older brother, Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, in the massive game in February 2023.

"For all the stars to align and for them to get through high school and college and the pros. And for them to both play in the Pro Bowl and to play in the Super Bowl, and then for this to happen," Donna told ET at the time. "This is just like a dream come true. I can't express enough how special this is for the family and it's just crazy.".

Donna, who was married to Ed for 25 years before they divorced, supported both of her sons by wearing a half-black, half-red Eagles and Chiefs jacket.

After the Super Bowl, which saw the Chiefs best the Eagles, Travis and Jason got emotional while reflecting on sharing the experience with Donna.

"The moment I saw mom is when I got really emotional," Jason stated on the brothers' New Heights podcast. "It was so awesome...She was on top of the world for a week.".

According to recent reports, "She was the heavyweight champ man," Travis added. "She was on top of it, and she shined the whole time.".

No. 7: He's Super-Close With His Brother.

Like Taylor and her younger brother Austin Swift, Travis has a special bond with his older brother Jason, who inspired him to play football.

In addition to their impressive careers as NFL players, Travis and Jason launched their podcast Newly introduced Heights in September 2022, a project that has only strengthened their relationship (and their bank accounts).

"What this did was gave us a scheduled two to three hour window where we have to talk to each other and we have to talk about what we're going through, throughout the week and throughout the games," Travis told NBC Sports in February 2023. "It's almost been like therapy, man.".

It has been revealed that no. 8: They Have a Mutual Friend.

Sure, the pair technically never met until 2023, but there have been a few invisible strings tying them together.

Taylor and Travis both count Miles Teller as a friend, with the Top Gun: Maverick star and his wife Keleigh Sperry even being recruited by Taylor to star in the music video for "I Bet You Think About Me" off Red (Taylor's Version) in 2021.

Travis, meanwhile, joined Miles and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for golfing practice ahead of the American Century Championship in 2022.

Miles tweeted a photo of himself on the golf course with the athletes, writing, "Grip it and rip it." Travis proved the bromance was real when he reposted the shot and added, "Back at it like we never left!!".

(Interestingly enough, Miles is a noted diehard Philadelphia Eagles fans, so perhaps he put in a word with Jason to broker an IRL meet-up between Travis and Taylor?).

While Taylor attended the Sept. 24, 2023 game solo, she brought an entourage of celebrity friends with her when she attended the Chiefs' match-up against the New York Jets at New Jersey's Metlife Stadium on Oct. 1.

She was accompanied by BFFs Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds and his friend Hugh Jackman, as well as Sophie Turner, Sabrina Carpenter and Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski.

While their attendance at the game spoke volumes, even more telling was Ryan following Travis on Instagram.

No. 10: He Can Handle the Pressure.

Not only has Travis played in four Super Bowls, winning three of them (NBD!), but he's also hosted Saturday Night Live, so you know he can handle intense spotlight with ease.

That may seem trivial, but Taylor has penned several songs regarding her fear that her level of fame could prove to be too much for her romantic partner to handle. (See: "Peace" and "The Archer.").

It has been revealed that "It all depends who you're with," Taylor stated in, "If they have a serious issue with it, I guess you'll hide or whatever, but I don't really like that, because it makes me feel like I'm running from the law or something. I don't want to feel like a fugitive, like, 'Oh my god, we're having a relationship, better hide!'.

"I feel like if you can be in a relationship and have it seem normal, that would be good.".

And in his WSJ interview, Travis proved he's more than ready for the pressure that comes with being married to someone as powerful as Taylor.

"Obviously I've never dated anyone with that kind of aura about them...I've never dealt with it," he stated. "But at the same time, I'm not running away from any of it.".

According to recent reports, "The scrutiny she gets, how much she has a magnifying glass on her, every single day, paparazzi outside her house, outside every restaurant she goes to, after every flight she gets off, and she's just living, enjoying life," he added. "When she acts like that I better not be the one acting all strange.".

No. 11: They Support One Another.

Sources indicate that further proving their love is worthy of a rom-com treatment, fans were swooning after a concertgoer captured video of Taylor running into Travis' arms and exchanging a passionate kiss after performing in Argentina in November 2023. And that was after she changed the lyrics in Karma from "the guy on the screen" to "the guy on the Chiefs," much to Travis' surprise as he attended alongside her father, Scott Swift.

Turning out for one another's stadium takeovers—Taylor attended 13 Chiefs games her first season with Travis, traveling straight from her Tokyo show to make the Super Bowl—is a show of how serious their relationship is.

"I'm going to see him do what he loves, we're showing up for each other, other people are there and we don't care," Taylor told TIME of their public support. "The opposite of that is you have to go to an extreme amount of effort to make sure no one knows that you're seeing someone. And we're just proud of each other.".

And if her presence at the NFL games annoys you, well, Taylor can't even be bothered to have bad blood with you.

In a recent development, "There's a camera, like, a half-mile away, and you don't know where it is, and you have no idea when the camera is putting you in the broadcast, so I don't know if I'm being shown 17 times or once," she remarked. "I'm just there to support Travis. I have no awareness of if I'm being shown too much and pissing off a few dads, Brads, and Chads.".

Travis was born in—are you ready for it?—1989. Screaming, crying, throwing up, etc.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of Killa Trav's birthday, which falls on October 5, did you know he shares his with Taylor's late grandmother Marjorie Finlay, the subject of her song "Marjorie" off of 2020's evermore? If we didn't know better, we'd think this is a sign...

She's loved him three summers now, honey, and she's going to get 'em all.

These are the animals people most want to see photographed

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Major Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo.
  • However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “Fresh Big Five” for wildlife photography.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability issues and to inspire positive action.

Originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Major Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “Fresh Big Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The Fresh Big 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green says that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on complications impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he says.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

Sources indicate that in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, says Green.

Sources indicate that “I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” says Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

According to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “Newly introduced Massive 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, says Green.

Industry observers note that as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “Latest Big 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” indicates Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, noted in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

According to recent reports, “I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she remarked.

“The Newly introduced Big 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of issues covered by the book.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ATEEZ earn their fourth No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart as GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 debuts atop the tally (dated Nov. 28). It’s the 10th top 10-charted project for the act, all of which have come since 2022. With the arrival, ATEEZ stand alone as the group with the most top 10s in the 2020s. Among all acts this decade, only YoungBoy Never Broke Again (15) and Taylor Swift (14) have more.

It has been revealed that GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 bows with 195,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the week ending Nov. 19, largely driven by pure album sales (191,000).

Also in the top 10, U2 collects its 14th top 10 as the band’s new studio album, Carnaval de Luz, debuts at No. 4.

The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Nov. 28, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard‘s website on Nov. 24. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X, formerly known as Twitter, and Instagram.

Of GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’s 195,000 first-week equivalent album units, album sales comprise 191,000 (it debuts at No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart), SEA units comprise 4,000 (equaling 4.04 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise a negligible sum.

ATEEZ have logged their 10 top 10s on the Billboard 200 consecutively. The act claimed its first top 10 with the No. 3-peaking THE WORLD EP.1 : MOVEMENT in 2022. In total, with 10 top 10s in the 2020s, ATEEZ now solely have the most top 10s among groups this decade. The act was previously tied with Stray Kids (which got its ninth top 10 — and ninth No. 1 — in August with This & That).

GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’s album sales were bolstered by its availability across 32 CD and vinyl variants (all containing collectible items such as photocards and posters, with some items randomized), including signed editions.

Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love falls to No. 2 on the latest Billboard 200 with 62,000 equivalent album units earned (down 1%). Morgan Wallen’s chart-topping I’m the Problem is a non-mover at No. 3 with a little more than 49,000 (up less than 1%).

U2 achieves its 14th top 10-charted album on the Billboard 200 as Carnaval de Luz debuts at No. 4 with 49,000 equivalent album units earned. Of that sum, album sales comprise 42,500 (it debuts at No. 2 on Top Album Sales), SEA units comprise 5,500 (equaling 5.77 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise 1,000.

U2 notched its first top 10 album on the Billboard 200 with the No. 1 The Joshua Tree in 1987 and was last in the top 10 with 2023’s Songs of Surrender (No. 5 debut and peak).

The fresh album’s first-week sales were aided by its availability across 18 physical variants (vinyl, CD, cassette and Blu-ray audio disc).

Carnaval de Luz was preceded by its lead single “Silencio,” which marked the group’s 45th entry on the Alternative Airplay chart earlier in November (tying Foo Fighters for the most in the chart’s history).

Two former No. 1s are next up on the Billboard 200, as Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide rises a spot to No. 5 (47,000 equivalent album units earned, up 8%) and Ella Langley’s Dandelion is pushed down 5-6 (45,000, up 2%). Kahan’s Stick Season is steady at No. 7 (36,000, up 2%) while SZA’s chart-topping SOS steps 9-8 (32,000, up 6%). Rounding out the top 10 are Olivia Dean’s The Art of Loving (down a spot to No. 9 with 32,000, down less than 1%) and Lil Baby’s FRESH (falling 2-10 with 31,000, down 47%).

Sources indicate that luminate, the independent data provider to the Billboard charts, completes a thorough review of all data submissions used in compiling the weekly chart rankings. Luminate reviews and authenticates data. In partnership with Billboard, data deemed suspicious or unverifiable is removed, using established criteria, before final chart calculations are made and published.

#70648. Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns

Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 exceptionally ancient quasars, including two that have set newly introduced records as the earliest ever observed.
  • Quasars are among the brightest objects in the cosmos.
  • Astronomers have spent decades searching for quasars from the Universe's earliest years because they offer valuable clues about the formation of the first galaxies and supermassive black holes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 exceptionally ancient quasars, including two that have set newly introduced records as the earliest ever observed. These brilliant galactic centers, powered by enormous black holes, were already radiating as much light as a trillion Suns when the Universe was only 670 million years old, about 5% of its present age.

Quasars are among the brightest objects in the cosmos. They appear during a relatively short period in a galaxy's history when huge quantities of gas and other material spiral toward its central supermassive black hole. This process releases extraordinary amounts of energy, causing the galaxy's core to shine hundreds or even thousands of times more brightly than the rest of the galaxy combined.

Astronomers have spent decades searching for quasars from the Universe's earliest years because they offer valuable clues about the formation of the first galaxies and supermassive black holes. Finding them, however, is extremely challenging. Few galaxies had grown large enough to host such objects at that early stage, and the light reaching us today is incredibly faint. These distant sources can also be difficult to distinguish from stars much closer to Earth.

Introduced in 2023, Euclid is transforming that search. Its ability to survey enormous regions of the sky and detect faint objects has already produced an unprecedented collection of 31 quasars from the early Universe, including some dating back to when the cosmos was just 5% of its current age.

"These early quasars date back to the Universe's infancy," says Daming Yang of Leiden University in the Netherlands, lead author of the Euclid discovery paper. "By finding and studying them, we can better understand how these enormous systems formed and grew so quickly - one of the greatest mysteries in astrophysics.".

Euclid Reveals a Hidden Population of Ancient Quasars.

Until now, astronomers had identified only a small fraction of the quasars that existed during the Universe's earliest period. Most known examples were exceptionally luminous objects that stood out because they were easier to detect. This limited sample made it difficult to understand the broader population and how these powerful systems developed.

According to recent reports, euclid is changing that picture by identifying not only the brightest quasars but also much fainter examples that previous searches struggled to find. Its discoveries are providing scientists with a far more representative view of the ancient quasar population, opening the door to more detailed studies of these early cosmic objects.

According to recent reports, "Euclid is a true game-changer," adds Daming. "Before, we could only find a handful of the very brightest ancient quasars, but Euclid lets us search far more efficiently across huge areas of sky to capture much fainter light. It's a unique tool for quasar hunting.".

It has been revealed that among the 31 newly identified quasars, 12 have a redshift of 7 or greater. Redshift describes how light is stretched as the Universe expands and helps astronomers determine how far away an object is and how far back in cosmic history its light originated. A redshift of at least 7 places these quasars within the Universe's first 770 million years.

Two Record-Breaking Quasars From Cosmic Dawn.

Recent findings suggest that two objects stand out as particularly extraordinary. The most ancient, EUCL J172902.75+641018.1, has a redshift of 7.77, while EUCL J125308.55+705432.3 has a redshift of 7.69. Both are located just over 13 billion light-years from Earth and were already shining within the first 670 million years of cosmic history.

These discoveries establish upcoming records for the earliest known quasars. The previous record belonged to an object discovered in 2021, which has a redshift of 7.64.

"This finding more than doubles the number of quasars we know of that are so ancient," claims Antonio La Marca, an ESA Research Fellow in the Euclid team.

It has been revealed that the pace of discovery is especially remarkable. Astronomers needed more than a decade to identify roughly the first 10 quasars with redshifts of 7 or higher. Euclid has already surpassed that number in just one year, demonstrating how dramatically the telescope is accelerating research into the early Universe.

In a recent development, "The Euclid team has taken a true 'census' of quasars at the dawn of the Universe for the first time," adds Antonio. "It's a significant step towards understanding these fascinating objects on a more fundamental level.".

Ancient Black Holes Reveal Clues About the First Galaxies.

One of the newly discovered objects is already offering additional insight into conditions during the Universe's infancy. Silvia Belladitta and colleagues recently conducted a more detailed investigation of the second most ancient quasar identified by Daming and his team.

Their observations revealed that the quasar sits inside a galaxy filled with gas and dust where newly introduced stars are forming at a tremendous rate. This provides an crucial glimpse of the environment surrounding an early supermassive black hole and could help researchers understand how the first massive galaxies evolved alongside the black holes at their centers.

These quasars also belong to a transformative chapter in cosmic history known as the epoch of reionization. During this period, the Universe emerged from a cold, dark state (the 'dark ages') as increasingly energetic radiation heated the surrounding gas and ionized it (split apart by energetic light). This fundamental transition helped establish the conditions that shaped the Universe we observe today.

"Ancient quasars are rare discoveries. They're interesting in themselves, but also time machines that enable us to explore the early Universe and understand how the first generation of galaxies came to be," claims ESA Euclid Project Scientist Valeria Pettorino.

How Euclid Is Transforming the Search for Cosmic Giants.

In a recent development, euclid's success comes from a powerful combination of capabilities. The telescope can examine enormous portions of the sky while collecting detailed images and detecting faint infrared light from extremely distant objects. Together, these features make it exceptionally effective at finding rare sources that earlier surveys could easily miss.

"Euclid's capabilities are unrivaled. The telescope combines a large area, depth, sharp imaging, and unique space-based infrared vision in a way that lets us pick out rare, extremely distant objects far more efficiently than before.

"And it's not just the telescope: the data processing is only possible thanks to thousands of Euclid Consortium scientists and engineers working together to deliver scientific discoveries, sifting through enormous datasets to identify rare, distant quasars that we can study further using telescopes on the ground.".

All 31 quasars were identified using observations from the Euclid Wide Survey, an ambitious project that will eventually examine more than one-third of the entire sky.

Sources indicate that although Euclid's primary mission is to investigate the dark Universe, its observations are revealing much more. By studying billions of galaxies, the telescope is helping astronomers investigate the Universe's composition, history, evolution, and vast cosmic structure. At the same time, its sweeping survey is uncovering rare ancient quasars that offer a remarkable opportunity to explore how the first galaxies and giant black holes emerged.

As Euclid continues mapping the cosmos, astronomers expect its growing collection of distant quasars to provide newly introduced clues about one of astrophysics' most enduring questions: how supermassive black holes became so enormous in such a remarkably short time after the Massive Bang.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past few years, WIRED has tested nearly every major brand of essential oil diffuser. Pura’s been our top nebulizer-style device (these work by blowing air through oil) for years due to its ease of use and sprawling library of high-end scents.

In a recent development, in fact, no brand even comes close to Pura's sheer breadth of available fragrances—with more than 150 options from significant names like Anthropologie, Nest, LAFCO, Brooklyn Candle Organization, Studio McGee, and more. Pura even has special seasonal collabs, like this month’s Nutcracker-inspired scents from the New York City Ballet. These diffusers are also highly convenient to use in that you can control them from your phone via an app (the Home, Plus, and Car also have buttons on the actual devices).

According to recent reports, but, it's a luxury you'll pay for. If you own a Pura or have seen it in stores, you already know the scents aren't cheap; single cartridges range from $14 for Pura’s house line all the way up to $21 for name brands like Thymes and Votivo. (The prices displayed on Pura's website look lower, but that's only if you buy a recurring subscription—make sure you note the one-time purchase price.).

Cartridges can last for a month or more in the Pura Mini, but in a larger diffuser like the Pura Plus, they may only last a couple of weeks. That's why the best time to stock up on scents for the year is during a sale, like Pura’s Cyber Week event. Right now through December 6, all fragrances are 20 percent off, and all diffusers are 30 percent off.

Recent findings suggest that pura's diffuser lineup isn't perfect, but neither are any of the diffusers we've tried from any brand. Diffusers can be loud or messy, take up a lot of space, or have an uninspiring line of scents. Pura's Mini and Car models are worthwhile yet quirky (though I can't recommend the Plus), but the Home has given me no issues in six months of testing.

If you're in the market for a Pura diffuser, our top pick for most people is the new Pura Home. The first Pura I ever owned was the 3 model, and I've also had the 4, but the 5 (rebranded “Home”) improves on just about everything, with dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz) Wi-Fi compatibility; faster diffusion; control buttons on the device itself; and even a new way to load cartridges, where you can slide out the bottom portion (which is flat to sit on a surface), seat the scents, and click it into place. QR codes on the cartridges inform your app which scents they are and when they were loaded, so it can, in turn, remind you when it's time to replace them. I also like that this model is totally silent.

In a recent development, I also recommend the oval-shaped Mini—I have one in my office right now. Though you can only control it via Pura's app, scents last for over a month, and it does a great job at scenting a smaller space like a bedroom. My unit makes a high-pitched ringing noise, almost like an ultrasonic pest repellent, which is annoying, but Pura's customer service will likely replace yours if this happens to you.

There’s also the Pura Car, whose refills I will be purchasing during this sale (MSRP averages $21 apiece, and the four-week run time has been roughly accurate in my experience). Online reviews of this device are mixed, but I love mine. If you’re a parent, having Pura scents to inhale instead of old, spilled food and stinky soccer cleats is 100 percent worth the spend. Buy one for a mom you know, but only if she has USB charging ports in her car—it needs to be plugged in most of the time, as it doesn’t hold a charge for very long.

Also on sale for 20 percent off is Pura's fun new Advent calendar, which features a Pura Home diffuser and 12 best-selling scents, most of which I have tried and can vouch for being options most people would enjoy.

Another Pura Cyber Week deal: Spend $50, and get 50 percent off the Pura Plus diffuser for large spaces, which has an MSRP of $80. I didn’t have the best of luck with the two Plus devices I went through—both eventually developed a loud buzzing noise. (Note that Pura will send you a replacement if this happens to you.) Additionally, unlike the Puras that sit flush to the outlet, this one is a cylinder that sits apart and must be plugged in at all times. It also makes an audible, fixed “shhhhhhh” noise as it’s long as it’s on (unlike the more intermittent noise emitted by competitors). However, it did do a great job of scenting a high-ceilinged room on the first floor of my house.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • flights delays eased on Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on track after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded departures nationwide for more than four hours on Friday.
  • According to recent reports, nearly 300 U.S.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over the weekend tied the concern that prompted officials to call for the ground stop to a router in southern Arkansas and work to update copper wires to a fiber-optic system overseen by L3Harris Technologies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, U.S. flights delays eased on Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on track after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded departures nationwide for more than four hours on Friday.

According to recent reports, nearly 300 U.S. flights were canceled and close to 1,000 were delayed Monday, a fraction of Sunday's disruptions, according to FlightAware data.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over the weekend tied the concern that prompted officials to call for the ground stop to a router in southern Arkansas and work to update copper wires to a fiber-optic system overseen by L3Harris Technologies. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford mentioned the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over to fiber optic.

Recent findings suggest that officials ordered the ground stop before 4 p.m. ET on Friday and it lasted until after 8 p.m. ET, marking the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

In a recent development, hundreds of thousands of travelers were stranded and about 18,000 U.S. flights were canceled from Friday through Monday morning, according to FlightAware.

According to recent reports, over that period, American Airlines had the most cancellations with 5,367 flights, close to 22% of its schedule, followed by Delta Air Lines with 3,434 cancellations, or 17% of its schedule, according to aviation data firm Cirium. Southwest Airlines and United Airlines each canceled more than 16% of their schedules. Bad weather on Thursday and Friday had also contributed to disruptions before the ground stop.

On Sunday, disruptions lingered but were starting to improve.

"We slept here," mentioned Beth Martin, who was trying to travel home to Birmingham, Alabama, from Latest York's LaGuardia Airport on Sunday at the end of her daughter's birthday trip. The two were booked for Saturday night, and when delay announcements started rolling in from Delta, they decided to make good use of the extra time: After strolling through Central Park, they went window shopping on Fifth Avenue.

But when the flight was canceled, the standby list for a backup flight looked grim and their original midtown hotel was charging about $700 for an additional night, the two slept at LaGuardia on Saturday. She remarked they found wheelchairs to sleep in outside security.

Airlines waived change fees and fare differences and offered pilots and flight attendants extra pay to ease the delays.

Customers told CNBC they were booked on several flights before getting on board.

Justine Fritz, who works in sales for a consumer goods manufacturer, was in Upcoming York for a business event on Friday. She tried five different flights before getting on one to Houston, then flew four hours out of her way to get back to Minneapolis after her Saturday flight was canceled. Fritz noted she had so many boarding passes that the Transportation Security Administration wouldn't let her through security at first.

"It's been bananas," she told CNBC at the gate. Fritz stated she made the best of it by shopping and getting a haircut, but she's still disappointed.

"I'm missing the first hour of the Vikings game," she said.

Martin noted her trip home with her daughter will take even longer. Delta booked them to Memphis, and her husband will drive the four hours from Birmingham to pick them up.

Officials are investigating the root cause that led to what the FAA described as "instability" in data feeds. Duffy said Sunday that two routers, the original one detected as a problem in southern Arkansas, and another in Amarillo, Texas, are in an L3Harris lab in Florida.

"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," L3Harris stated in a statement Saturday afternoon.

President Donald Trump stated Monday he didn't "take any responsibility" for the ground stop.

Shortly after the ground stop, Duffy noted he was asking Congress for as much as $50 billion for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system. A day later, Democratic lawmakers pushed back, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

"Our committee, on behalf of the flying public, will hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again," mentioned Reps. Rick Larsen, D.-Wash., ranking member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and Andre Carson, D.-Ind., ranking member of the aviation subcommittee, in a joint statement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the second day of Corona Capital 2026 on Saturday (Nov. 21) brought back Twenty One Pilots as the headlining act of the renowned Mexican festival. The duo made up of vocalist Tyler Joseph and drummer Josh Dun performed their final concert of the year in Mexico City, which also marked their last show before an indefinite hiatus, as they indicated during their set. The show turned into a nostalgic and emotional moment, underscoring the deep connection they’ve built with their local fans over the years.

On its second day, the music fest gathered approximately 76,000 attendees, according to promoter Ocesa, who enjoyed a diverse lineup of performances, ranging from the energetic ’90s punk of The Offspring and the wild post-hardcore of Pierce the Veil to more subtle moments from the Greek artist Σtella and the refined electronic and French touch of Sebastien Tellier.

Canadian punk artist Peaches captivated the crowd with her irreverence and queer activism, while her fellow Canadians in Mother Mother delivered one of the most celebrated moments of the night with their alternative rock set, which included covers of classics like Nirvana’s “In Bloom” and Pixies’ “Where Is My Mind?”.

The British electronic duo Underworld made their first appearance in the Latin American country in seven years, transforming the Corona Cero stage into a massive dance floor with their iconic track “Born Slippy.” Other stages set up at the Curva 4, the site of Mexico City’s Formula 1 Grand Prix, also hosted performances by DOPE LEMON, Baby Queen, We Are Scientists, Militarie Gun, Maisie Peters, Strawberry Guy and Princess Chelsea, among others.

Industry observers note that the program continued on Sunday (Nov. 22) with headliners The Strokes, the Mexican debut of Canadian experimental math-rock duo Angine de Poitrine and the veteran Welsh rock band Manic Street Preachers. Other acts on the Sunday lineup: The Black Crowes, Johnny Marr, Lola Young, Lil Yachty, Tipling Rock, Tricky and the highly anticipated return of The xx.

In a recent development, below are five of our favorite moments from Day 2 of the Corona Capital 2026 festival. Check out the highlights from Day 1 here.

Industry observers note that the duo made up of vocalist Tyler Joseph and drummer Josh Dun returned to Corona Capital after five years to deliver their final show before taking an indefinite break from the stage. Before performing “Trees,” Joseph gave an emotional message to their fans, who had already danced and sung along to tracks like “Overcompensate,” “The Contract,” “Center Mass,” “Jumpsuit” and “Nico and the Niners.”.

“It’s our last song, our last show of the year, actually. It’s our last show for a while,” the vocalist said. “And I’m not just saying this to you, which I do mean it, for you in front of me right now but anybody else who sees this: you’ve changed our lives. Thank you so much for believing in this music, believing in live music, coming to indicates. I’ve run out of ways to say thank you.”.

Sources indicate that the Ohio-based duo fulfilled the dream of Rodrigo, one of their fans, by inviting him on stage to sing “Ride” with them. Another highlight was a cover of The White Stripes’ “Seven Nation Army.”.

California-based band The Offspring brought all their punk energy to the second day of the festival, performing major hits like “Come Out and Play,” “Why Don’t You Get a Job?,” “Pretty Fly (For a White Guy)” and “The Kids Aren’t Alright,” as well as covers like Taylor Swift’s “Love Story.”.

The crowd fully embraced the band, led by vocalist Dexter Holland, chanting “Olé, olé, olé” along to the rhythm. Fans also celebrated its tribute to the late Ozzy Osbourne with renditions of Black Sabbath classics “Crazy Train” and “Paranoid.”.

To the rhythm of legendary singer-songwriter José Alfredo Jiménez and his iconic ranchera song “El Rey,” the band from San Diego, California, took the main stage to deliver one of the wildest performances of the festival with their post-hardcore sound on Saturday night.

The moshpit ruled the main stage to the beat of songs like “May These Noises Startle You in Your Sleep Tonight,” “Hell Above,” “Caraphernelia,” “Bulls in the Bronx” and “I’d Rather Die Than Be Famous.” The group, founded by vocalist and guitarist Vic Fuentes, also performed a cover of Pixies’ “Where Is My Mind?,” which had already been played earlier on the Doritos stage by Mother Mother.

Recent findings suggest that the Canadian artist took electroclash, industrial beats and provocation to the limit, turning her performance into a celebration of chaos, dance and freedom. With her trademark irreverence, Peaches wore a bodysuit adorned with faux hair on the breasts and genital area to advocate for trans women’s rights. Her performance became a full-fledged display of activism, featuring messages in support of Palestine and punk music, leaving an indelible mark on the memory of those who witnessed this unique moment.

Ryan Guldemond, guitarist and lead singer of the Canadian indie rock band Mother Mother, confessed to the audience that he thought their presence on one of the festival’s main stages was a mistake, especially since they had a primetime slot. Nonetheless, he admitted that performing at Corona Capital was a dream come true.

The band delighted the crowd with a set that included their upcoming song “Rot,” as well as hits from their repertoire like “The Sticks,” “Verbatim,” “Make Believe” and “Hayloft.” They also created a special moment for their fans by performing covers of Nirvana’s “In Bloom” and Pixies’ “Where Is My Mind?”.

#70642. Breaking: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression

Breaking: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A consistent daily routine may do more for your health than you realize.
  • The findings suggest that everyday habits, such as waking up, eating meals, socializing, and going to bed at consistent times, may play an crucial role in physical and mental well-being.
  • It has been revealed that the discovery could be especially crucial for older adults, who frequently experience sleep difficulties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A consistent daily routine may do more for your health than you realize. Researchers at the University of Missouri have found that older adults who follow regular daily schedules tend to experience less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggle to get a good night's sleep.

The findings suggest that everyday habits, such as waking up, eating meals, socializing, and going to bed at consistent times, may play an crucial role in physical and mental well-being. By helping the body maintain its natural internal clock, a predictable routine could offer health benefits that extend beyond improved sleep.

It has been revealed that the discovery could be especially crucial for older adults, who frequently experience sleep difficulties. According to the National Council on Aging, roughly half of adults age 60 and older report symptoms of insomnia, a condition that can make it difficult to fall asleep, stay asleep, or get restful sleep.

Daily Routines Linked to Less Pain and Depression.

According to recent reports, to investigate the relationship between sleep, daily habits, and overall health, Eunjin Tracy, an assistant professor in the College of Education and Human Development at the University of Missouri, examined survey responses from 67 older adults. Among the participants, 37 reported experiencing insomnia.

As researchers expected, those with insomnia generally reported more physical pain and higher levels of depression than participants without the condition. However, another pattern emerged when Tracy examined their daily routines.

Sources indicate that participants who maintained more consistent schedules tended to report less pain and fewer depressive symptoms, regardless of their sleep quality. This suggests that keeping regular daily habits may be associated with better health even when sleep problems persist.

"Regardless of sleep quality, those who reported having a regular daily routine had lower levels of physical pain and less depression compared to those without a daily routine," Tracy noted. "If we are consistent with when we wake up, eat, work or study, interact with others and go to bed, those time cues help synchronize our internal body clocks. Over the long term, that seems to be linked with improved health outcomes.".

Why Your Body's Internal Clock Matters.

One possible explanation involves the circadian rhythm, the body's natural 24-hour timing system. This internal clock helps coordinate when we feel awake or sleepy and influences numerous biological processes, including hormone activity, metabolism, and mood.

Rather than operating independently of our surroundings, the circadian system responds to signals that help it keep time. Light and darkness are especially crucial, but regular activities such as eating, working, interacting with others, and sleeping can also provide timing cues.

Recent findings suggest that when these signals follow a predictable pattern, they help keep the body's biological rhythms aligned. Irregular schedules, on the other hand, can interfere with that coordination.

"When we regulate our circadian rhythm well, our bodies function well, but if it gets too distracted, our bodies don't function as well," Tracy said.

Although the study did not establish that regular routines directly reduce pain or depression, the findings point to circadian regulation as one possible explanation for the connection.

The Hidden Effects of Social Jet Lag.

Industry observers note that even relatively small changes in daily schedules may disrupt the body's internal clock. One common example is social jet lag, which occurs when a person's sleep schedule shifts between workdays and days off.

Sources indicate that someone who wakes up early throughout the week but stays up late and sleeps in on weekends may experience this mismatch. The resulting disruption resembles some of the effects of traveling across time zones, even though the person has never left home.

Tracy suggests that maintaining reasonably consistent schedules throughout the entire week, including weekends, may help limit these disruptions and support healthier circadian rhythms.

"As someone who wakes up and goes to bed at the same time every day, I think a daily routine can be helpful for people of all ages across their lifespan," Tracy stated. "There is growing awareness about the concept of social jet lag -- waking up and going to bed at different times on weekends compared to weekdays -- and the disruptions it causes to our circadian rhythm, so hopefully this research helps more people consider the health benefits of a daily routine. Since one-third of our lives will be spent sleeping, I think health and well-being research should be looked at holistically from a 24-hour perspective and not just focus on when we are awake.".

A Simple Habit With Potential Health Benefits.

The research highlights an aspect of healthy living that can be easy to overlook. While getting enough quality sleep remains crucial, the consistency of activities throughout the day may also be connected to how people feel physically and emotionally.

Because the study relied on survey data from a relatively small group of older adults, it cannot prove that adopting a regular routine will relieve pain or depression. Larger studies would be needed to establish whether changing daily schedules directly improves these outcomes.

Still, the findings suggest that a predictable daily routine may be a useful component of a broader approach to health, particularly for people experiencing insomnia.

For older adults and potentially people of other ages, simple habits such as maintaining regular waking times, eating meals on a consistent schedule, and limiting major changes in weekend sleep patterns may help support the body's natural rhythms.

The study, "Behavioral-social rhythms and insomnia symptoms: associations with pain, body mass index, and depressive symptoms among older adults," was published in the Journal of Behavioral Medicine.

GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time.
  • To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs).
  • In a recent development, the frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time. Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans?

To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space.

In a recent development, the frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons.

The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games.

With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars.

Recent findings suggest that massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics.

Starfield even has a "fresh game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it.

The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining.

Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky.

According to recent reports, it's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns with alien NPCs, gigantic kaiju-like beasts, and... fishing. The endless free updates have pushed the roleplaying aspects deeper, as Hello Games are really making it the "forever" space game.

In a recent development, most importantly though, you can be the greatest bad guy the virtually infinite universe has ever seen, controlling entire pirate fleets and firing on (or stealing) every spaceship that you come across. It might be a bit aimless for some, but if you love a "forever game" then NMS can be the biggest space-set criminal sim ever created.

Though it took too long, Star Wars has gotten really close to cracking the GTA formula in outer space in a shameless enough way. 2024's Star Wars Outlaws is, to this date, the closest thing we've received to a space-set sandbox directly inspired by Rockstar's huge hits.

It has been revealed that by letting us fully embrace the Han Solo-like scoundrel fantasy, Massive Entertainment delivered a Star Wars adventure that's all about breaking the law. Hell, they even got a wanted system in there that has protagonist Kay Vess dodging stormtroopers and rival criminal factions like you would in Vice City.

Star Wars Outlaws' take on GTA isn't just about the surface-level gameplay and open structure; it also understands much of its playful tone, moral ambiguity, and stressful rhythm. Jumping between several medium-sized maps set on different planets and spaceship sections breaks up the experience a little, so it never quite reaches that level of seamless immersion, but if anyone wants to do a focused version of GTA in space in the future, Massive's attempt is the one game that got at least halfway there.

Before we go (and before you go back to playing GTA VI), we should remember the daring video games that, for a variety of reasons, never got to realize their visions of a crime-oriented space adventure.

Recent findings suggest that remember Star Wars 1313 and Visceral Games' cancelled project? It's hard not to spot some of their DNA surviving in Outlaws. As Luke Skywalker wisely noted before noping out, "No one's ever really gone." Lucasfilm loves that, and it extends to binned video games too, thankfully. Even the elusive Battlefront 3 is back from the dead now.

Bethesda also had something going at some point with "Prey 2", a bounty hunter action game set in a cyberpunk-ish alien world. Before it was canned, it dropped one of the coolest CG game trailers ever made and teased us with a Blade Runner-esque future long before Cyberpunk hit our consoles.

Looking at the future, Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 wants to go big and lawless, potentially iterating on Star Wars Outlaws and other open-world crime sims. But years after its announcement and many mind-boggling development news updates, it's hard to believe it's really ever coming out. Maybe the "Before GTA VI" meme can morph into "Before BG&E2" now that Rockstar's masterpiece is finally out.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Rockstar is Rockstar. A one-of-a-kind megastudio with nearly unlimited resources. Trying to replicate GTA does — either on Earth or among the stars — would be an Icarus flight in the making for most studios. There are some GTA-flavored space adventures out there, as we've shown, but we're still waiting for the one. Something that matches the deep storytelling, complete freedom, and cheeky tone of Rockstar's iconic series. OK, I gotta get out of here, I'm too hip for this, I gotta play GTA VI some more.

Industry observers note that jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.

Recent findings suggest that fran Ruiz is our resident Star Wars guy. His hunger for movies and TV series is only matched by his love for video games. He also serves as associate editor over at Star Wars News Net and its sister site, Movie News Net.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve. It will be the 26th James Bond film and the first since Amazon MGM took over the iconic franchise.

According to recent reports, pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role. Monday's announcement — which came in part via an Instagram post — ends a long period of speculation about who would take over as "007" after Daniel Craig.

Industry observers note that "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.".

Pattinson has appeared in several substantial-ticket films this year, including Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" and psychological thriller "Primetime," and he'll soon appear in "Dune: Part Three," also directed by Villeneuve. Pattinson, who rose to fame with the Twilight movie series, is also in production for Matt Reeves' "The Batman Part II," a follow-up to the 2022 film based on the DC comic.

The upcoming Bond film will have a script by Steven Knight and will be produced by Amy Pascal, known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, and David Heyman, who produced all eight Harry Potter films.

"We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Villeneuve said. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.".

Recent findings suggest that in 2022, Amazon bought MGM Studios, which had long produced the Bond movies, for roughly $8.45 billion. Amazon MGM then acquired creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights in 2025, when it closed a deal with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

The film is still untitled, and Amazon MGM hasn't confirmed a projected release date.

#70638. A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1823 w)

A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A common amino acid found in everyday foods could play a surprisingly key role in helping the immune system recognize cancer and fight viral infections.
  • Sources indicate that arginine is an amino acid that the body produces naturally and also obtains from protein-rich foods.
  • Now, new research suggests that restoring arginine levels could help the immune system respond more effectively to serious threats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A common amino acid found in everyday foods could play a surprisingly key role in helping the immune system recognize cancer and fight viral infections. Scientists at Rockefeller University have discovered that when the body runs low on arginine, a key part of its immune defense system can stop working properly, potentially allowing dangerous cells and viruses to escape detection.

Sources indicate that arginine is an amino acid that the body produces naturally and also obtains from protein-rich foods. It is essential for making proteins that perform countless functions throughout the body. Researchers have long known that unusually low arginine levels are associated with several diseases, including colon cancer, but exactly how this shortage affects the body's defenses has remained unclear.

Now, new research suggests that restoring arginine levels could help the immune system respond more effectively to serious threats. In experiments involving mice, increasing dietary arginine reduced the formation of colon cancer tumors and lessened the severity of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infections. Remarkably, providing arginine after mice had already contracted influenza also improved their outcomes.

The findings, published in the journal Cell, raise the possibility that an inexpensive, readily available supplement could eventually become a useful addition to cancer treatments and strategies for combating viral infections. However, further research in humans is needed to determine whether the benefits observed in mice translate into effective treatments for people.

How a Missing Nutrient Could Help Cancer Escape the Immune System.

Industry observers note that the research was led by Sohail Tavazoie, who directs the Elizabeth and Vincent Meyer Laboratory of Systems Cancer Biology at Rockefeller University. His team has spent years investigating how arginine influences cancer development and progression.

In 2023, the researchers discovered that depriving colon cancer cells of arginine caused them to accumulate more genetic mutations. These changes can contribute to the unpredictable behavior of cancer cells, raising important questions about how arginine shortages might influence the disease.

Industry observers note that the latest study reveals another potentially significant consequence. When arginine becomes scarce, cells struggle to produce enough of a crucial immune system protein known as MHC-1. This protein acts as a warning system, helping immune cells identify potential dangers such as cancerous changes or viral infections.

Without enough MHC-1, abnormal or infected cells may become harder for the immune system to recognize.

Encouragingly, the researchers also found that supplying a moderate amount of arginine, comparable to the quantity available in a couple of over-the-counter supplement tablets, could help restore production of this notable protein.

Recent findings suggest that "Our work reveals how a lack of arginine interferes with the immune system, and suggests that upping arginine intake could prove beneficial," says first author Qiushuang Wu, a postdoc in the lab. "Perhaps that means it could be used in combination with other therapies to treat both cancer and viral infections.".

Recent findings suggest that "Arginine supplementation could be readily tested in patients receiving immunotherapies or given to high-risk populations exposed to viral pathogens," Tavazoie suggests. "Considering that arginine is inexpensive and readily available, we hope that therapeutic and preventative studies could be undertaken soon.".

The Surprising Connection Between Arginine and Immune Defenses.

To understand why arginine has such an key effect, the researchers investigated how cells use amino acids to manufacture proteins.

Sources indicate that proteins are built from amino acids according to genetic instructions encoded in DNA. These instructions are copied into messenger RNA, which carries the information to the cellular machinery responsible for protein production.

It has been revealed that the instructions are read in groups of three genetic letters called codons. Each codon specifies an amino acid or provides another signal needed during protein production. Arginine is unusual in that six different codons can specify it, reflecting the multiple ways its incorporation into proteins can be encoded.

Industry observers note that scientists already knew that changes in amino acid availability could affect cellular metabolism and signaling, two processes that help regulate how cells obtain energy and respond to their surroundings. What remained less clear was whether shortages of particular amino acids could directly influence which proteins cells produce.

To investigate, Wu examined the effects of arginine availability across several disease models, including colon cancer, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2. Each of these diseases has previously been associated with abnormal levels of various amino acids.

The research was supported in part by the Stavros Niarchos Foundation (SNF) Institute for Global Infectious Disease Research at The Rockefeller University and the Weill Cancer East Hub.

"One of the most dramatic patterns to emerge was that arginine was the most depleted amino acid in all of these diseases," she states.

Why Low Arginine Levels Can Disrupt the Immune System.

Industry observers note that in laboratory experiments using cultured cells, Wu examined how arginine shortages affected protein production. She identified 414 proteins whose levels dropped abnormally when arginine was scarce.

Industry observers note that many of these proteins were associated with biological functions already known to depend on arginine. However, the researchers uncovered a more unexpected effect involving three genes from the HLA family.

These genes provide instructions for producing proteins associated with MHC-I (major histocompatibility complex class I), an essential component of the immune system's ability to recognize threats.

It has been revealed that MHC-I proteins are displayed on the surfaces of cells throughout the body. They act somewhat like identification displays, presenting small fragments of proteins from inside the cell to immune cells known as T cells.

When these displays reveal suspicious material, such as proteins produced by a virus or abnormal proteins associated with cancer, T cells can recognize the danger and help coordinate an immune response.

But the researchers found that arginine deficiency interfered with the production of these molecular warning signals.

The reason involved ribosomes, the tiny cellular machines that assemble proteins by following genetic instructions. Because the proteins involved in MHC-I production require arginine at numerous points, the researchers suspected that an insufficient supply could interfere with their assembly.

Further experiments confirmed that suspicion. When arginine was unavailable, ribosomes stalled while trying to manufacture MHC-I proteins. Without enough of the required amino acid, the cells could not efficiently complete the process.

According to recent reports, as a result, fewer MHC-I proteins reached the cell surface, reducing the signals that would normally alert T cells to cancer-associated or viral proteins. This created an opportunity for dangerous cells to avoid immune detection.

"These findings are exciting because they reveal that consumption of a specific amino acid can directly regulate gene expression in an organism by increasing production of a protein enriched in that amino acid," Tavazoie says. "We believe that such selective translational tuning of gene expression through dietary manipulation likely extends to many other proteins and amino acids.".

More Arginine Meant Fewer Colon Cancer Tumors in Mice.

After identifying the molecular mechanism, Wu investigated whether changing the amount of arginine in an animal's diet could influence disease outcomes.

Sources indicate that mice receiving diets low in arginine developed more colon cancer tumors. In contrast, mice consuming higher amounts of the amino acid developed fewer tumors.

These findings provided evidence that arginine availability can influence cancer development through its effects on the immune system, rather than simply changing how individual cancer cells behave.

The results also raised a broader question: If arginine helps immune cells recognize cancer, could it provide similar benefits when the body encounters dangerous viruses?

Arginine Also Improved Outcomes From Influenza and COVID-19 Viruses.

To explore that possibility, Wu collaborated with Heinz-Heinrich Hoffman, a research assistant professor in Charles Rice's Laboratory of Virology and Infectious Disease.

Together, they examined the effects of dietary arginine in mouse models of influenza and SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19.

The findings followed the same general pattern seen in the colon cancer experiments. Mice consuming more arginine experienced less severe symptoms from viral infections, suggesting that adequate levels of the amino acid helped support the body's immune defenses.

The researchers then made an even more surprising discovery.

Arginine did not appear to be beneficial only when consumed before an infection. Giving mice additional arginine after they had already been infected with influenza also improved their outcomes.

"Not only did mice with an arginine-rich diet have milder symptoms from viral infections, giving the mice arginine after influenza infection improved their outcomes too," Wu notes. "That was very surprising. From our genetic models, we knew manipulating arginine levels had a strong effect on gene expression, but we didn't expect the dietary manipulation to be equally impactful.".

The observation suggests that changing nutrient availability might influence how the immune system responds even after a viral infection has taken hold.

Could a Simple Supplement Improve Cancer and Virus Treatments?

The discovery has potentially vital implications for understanding why some people become more vulnerable to cancer and severe viral infections.

Arginine levels naturally decline with age, and inadequate nutrition can further reduce the amount available to cells. The researchers suspect that these changes may contribute to the weakening of immune defenses seen in certain diseases and in older adults.

"Qiushuang's findings illuminate how poor diet and aging -- during which arginine levels naturally decline -- could create the perfect storm for the initiation of colon cancer. Similarly, age-related arginine loss could partially contribute to the greater mortality caused by respiratory viruses," Tavazoie notes. "We're also investigating whether making dietary changes in other amino acids has beneficial effects in a variety of disease contexts. There are no doubt more discoveries to come.".

In a recent development, the possibility of using arginine alongside existing cancer immunotherapies is particularly intriguing. These treatments work by helping the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells. If low arginine levels interfere with the molecular signals required for that recognition, restoring the nutrient might help some treatments work more effectively.

The researchers also see potential for investigating arginine supplementation in people at elevated risk of respiratory viral infections.

It has been revealed that for now, these possibilities remain experimental. The findings do not establish that taking arginine supplements prevents or treats cancer, influenza, or COVID-19 in humans.

Nevertheless, the research reveals an important connection between nutrition and immunity. Rather than simply providing the raw materials needed to build proteins, specific amino acids may help determine how effectively the body's immune defenses identify and respond to dangerous threats.

And because arginine is inexpensive and widely available, the discovery could provide a practical starting point for future studies aimed at strengthening the immune system against cancer and infectious diseases.

#70636. Don’t Bring Jensen Back

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1320 w)
